_strings.@@1a635cc8f9e6: Credit for Child and Dependent Care Expenses (Rhode Island portion of the allowable federal credit) — Taxpayers who claimed the federal Credit for Child and Dependent Care Expenses (federal Form 1040/1040-SR, Schedule 3, line 2). Rhode Island allows a credit equal to a percentage of that federal care credit, limited to the amount of Rhode Island income tax (so any excess is not refunded - it is nonrefundable).

_strings.@@604678a0c96f: Property Tax Relief Credit (Form RI-1040H, the RI property-tax "circuit breaker") — Must answer YES to ALL eligibility questions on Form RI-1040H Part 1: (A) domiciled in Rhode Island for all of 2024; (B) lived in a household or rented a dwelling that was subject to property tax in 2024; (C) current on property taxes or rent due on the homestead for 2024 and all prior years; (D) you OR your spouse were 65 years of age or older AND/OR disabled as of December 31, 2024; and (E) 2024 total household income was $39,275 or less. Both homeowners (attach 2024 property tax bill) and renters (attach 2024 lease or rent receipts; rent paid is multiplied by 20% as deemed property tax) may claim it.
_strings.@@79259222a811: Credit for Income Taxes Paid to Another State — Rhode Island residents who also paid income tax to another state on income that is also taxed by Rhode Island. Authorized under R.I. Gen. Laws section 44-30-18. If income tax was paid to more than one other state, Form RI-1040MU must be used (a separate calculation for each state); a signed copy of each other-state return must be attached.
_strings.@@97e03350195a: Treaty conformity — RI conforms to federal treaty treatment — income exempt from federal tax under a treaty is also excluded from RI income (it flows through the federal starting point; do not add it back on the RI return). (This is about TREATY conformity only — a state can conform on treaties while DECOUPLING from the federal Code for deductions or credits; see any law-change lines below.) State note: The RI-1040 resident return starts from federal adjusted gross income (2024 RI-1040 Line 1: "Federal AGI (Federal Form 1040 or 1040-SR, line 11)"; instructions Line 1: "Enter your federal adjusted gross income from Federal Form 1040 or Federal Form 1040-SR, line 11"), and the General Instructions state "the Rhode Island income tax is based on your federal adjusted gross income." RI taxable income is built only via the RI Schedule M modifications. The 2024 "Modifications Increasing Federal Adjusted Gross Income" on Schedule M are: out-of-state municipal bond interest (2a), RI fiduciary adjustment (2b), recapture of Family Education Account modifications (2c), bonus depreciation (2d), recapture of Tuition Savings Program/Section 529 modifications (2e), recapture of previously-claimed tax-credit income (2f), recapture of Scituate Medical Savings Account modifications (2g), pass-through entity tax taken as a federal deduction (2h), unemployment compensation not included in federal AGI (2i), taxable Paycheck Protection Program loan amount (2j), and a reserved line (2k). NONE of these add back income that is exempt from federal tax under a U.S. income tax treaty. Because treaty-exempt income is already excluded from federal AGI and RI has no add-back of it, it flows through and is not re-taxed by Rhode Island. Therefore RI conforms (treaty-exempt income is not re-taxed).
_strings.@@c04c25c00335: Form RI-1040NR (Rhode Island Nonresident Individual Income Tax Return) — nonresidents complete RI Schedule II; part-year residents complete RI Schedule III
_strings.@@e6d78583de79: Rhode Island Earned Income Credit (RI EITC) — Resident (and part-year/eligible nonresident) taxpayers who qualify for and claim the FEDERAL Earned Income Tax Credit. RI does not impose its own separate eligibility test - if you receive the federal EITC, you receive the RI EITC. You must claim the federal EITC (federal Form 1040/1040-SR, line 27) to claim the RI credit.
_strings.@@eb71823a243b: Multi-state income allocation (which dollars belong to which state) is your and the user's judgment; this tool scopes the returns and supplies the rules/warnings, not the allocation.

Corroborated by: 2024 Instructions for Filing RI-1040 (updated 12/09/2024), Line 4 standard deduction list and Line 6 exemption amount $4,950, and p. I-11 RHODE ISLAND TAX COMPUTATION WORKSHEET (3.75% / subtract $0.00, 4.75% / subtract $774.50, 5.99% / subtract $2,957.52) at https://tax.ri.gov/sites/g/files/xkgbur541/files/2024-12/2024%201040R%20Instructions%20-%20updated%2012092024.pdf; 2024 Rhode Island Tax Table booklet page T-1 (tax-table mandate under $100,000) at https://tax.ri.gov/sites/g/files/xkgbur541/files/2024-12/2024%20RI%20Tax%20Tables_Complete.pdf; 2024 Form RI-1040 page 1 (Lines 1-8) at https://tax.ri.gov/sites/g/files/xkgbur541/files/2024-12/2024_1040WE_w.pdf — both passes agree.

state_tax.work_common_tail: . Tax line: RI-1040, Line 8: "RI income tax from Rhode Island Tax Table or Tax Computation Worksheet" (Line 7 "RI TAXABLE INCOME. Subtract line 6 from line 5. If zero or less, enter 0"; Line 5 = Line 3 modified federal AGI minus Line 4 RI standard deduction; Line 6 = number of exemptions x $4,950) This op computes the state's rate-schedule tax line ONLY — county/city add-on taxes, state credits, and any amounts outside the rate schedule are NOT modeled. Pack notes: Base guidance: Supply 2024 Form RI-1040, Line 3 'Modified Federal AGI' (Line 1 federal AGI from Federal Form 1040 or 1040-SR, line 11, combined with Line 2 net modifications from RI Schedule M; with no modifications Line 3 equals federal AGI). Do NOT subtract anything yourself: the op subtracts the shipped RI standard deduction (Line 4) and the shipped $4,950-per-person exemptions (Line 6) to reach RI TAXABLE INCOME (Line 7), then applies the rate schedule. Adjudication note (two-pass): base is federal_agi — RI-1040 starts from federal AGI (line 1) and taxable_base is Line 3 modified federal AGI (federal AGI +/- RI Schedule M modifications); the op subtracts the standard deduction and $4,950-per-exemption Line 6 amount. 2024 indexation: the three-bracket structure is unchanged from 2023; the breakpoints rose to $77,450/$176,050 (from $73,450/$166,950), the standard deduction to $10,550/$21,150/$10,575/$15,850, the exemption to $4,950 (from $4,700), and the phaseout threshold to $246,450 (from $233,750) — all from the December 2024 official rate-and-worksheets page. Single rate schedule for every filing status: the 2024 Rhode Island Tax Rate Schedule is captioned 'FOR ALL FILING STATUS TYPES' — the same three brackets (3.75% to $77,450; 4.75% to $176,050; 5.99% above) apply to Single, MFJ, MFS, HoH, and Qualifying widow(er); the schedule is duplicated per status here. Qualifying widow(er)/surviving spouse maps to married_filing_jointly: the RI standard deduction chart lists Qualifying widow(er) at the same $21,150 as MFJ, so the mapping is exact. Tax-table mandate below $100,000: the 2024 RI Tax Table booklet instructs 'if your taxable income is less than $100,000 use the Rhode Island Tax Table... If your taxable income is larger than $100,000, use the Rhode Island Tax Computation Worksheet.' The table uses $50 bands computed at the band midpoint (e.g. taxable income $25,300-$25,350 yields tax $950 = $25,325 x 3.75% rounded), so bracket math may differ by a few dollars within table bands; the filed form must use the table below $100,000. Standard-deduction and exemption PHASEOUT is NOT modeled: if RI-1040 Line 3 (modified federal AGI) exceeds $246,450, BOTH the standard deduction and the $4,950 exemptions phase down in 20-percentage-point steps (factors 0.8000/0.6000/0.4000/0.2000) per $7,050 increment of the excess (rounded up to a whole increment), and both are $0 once the excess is more than $28,200 (i.e. Line 3 above $274,650). This op ships the full amounts — taxpayers with Line 3 over $246,450 must use the Standard Deduction Worksheet and Exemption Worksheet from the 2024 RI Tax Rate Schedule and Worksheets page instead. Rhode Island does not allow the use of federal itemized deductions (2024 RI-1040 instructions, Line 4) — every filer takes the RI standard deduction shipped here; there is no itemized alternative to model. If someone else can claim you as a dependent on their return, your RI exemption amount is zero (2024 RI-1040 instructions, Line 6 NOTE) — not modeled; such filers should be computed with zero exemptions. taxable_base must be RI-1040 Line 3 (Modified Federal AGI = federal AGI plus/minus net RI Schedule M modifications). Schedule M modifications (e.g. out-of-state municipal bond interest add-back, US-government-interest subtraction, taxable-Social-Security and pension/annuity modifications, military service pension modification) are NOT computed by this op; with no modifications Line 3 equals federal AGI (Federal Form 1040/1040-SR, line 11). Printed-constant rounding in the rate schedule: the 'Pay' constants are rounded to the cent and each diverges from the exact cumulative bracket sum by +$0.005 — printed $2,904.38 vs exact $2,904.375 (3.75% x $77,450), and printed $7,587.88 vs exact $7,587.875. By contrast, RI's credits — the 16% RI earned income credit for 2024 (Line 14d, RI Schedule EIC line 41), 25% of the federal child and dependent care credit (RI Schedule I, carried to Line 9a), credit for taxes paid to other states (Line 9b), the RI-1040H property-tax relief circuit breaker (Line 14c, max $675 for 2024) — are subtracted from TAX, not income, and are NOT applied by this op.
